title: Autosentinel fallback signal attribution and circuit recovery playbook
creator: Priya Nair
description: Problem: our smart routing stack must detect overload and failure modes (429s, timeouts, elevated error rates) and automatically route traffic to safer model variants or alternative regions/tiers. Existing rules are threshold-heavy and produce noisy flip-flops for noisy signals and slow-recovery tenants. Goal: implement an autosentinel system that attributes which signal(s) (region, tier, model variant, upstream infra) caused the degradation, triggers a graded circuit/fallback action, and drives an automated recovery procedure with hysteresis and dark-probing to validate restoration before full reopen.
acceptance_criteria: Autosentinel identifies the dominant signal source (region|tier|model variant|tenant) for at least 90% of degradation windows in replay tests
Fallback actions (soft degrade to lower-tier model, regional handover, or rate-limit) execute within configured latency SLO and do not increase 5xx rate by >2% in rollback windows
Circuit opens/soft-fails using calibrated hysteresis and decay windows; automated dark-probes validate recovery before reopening
New dashboards show per-signal trip score, action taken, and end-to-end request path for post-mortem analysis
Integration tests simulate 429 storm and timeout cascades and demonstrate stable behavior across 10 runs without oscillation
proposed_design: Signal fusion: compute per-tenant, per-region, per-tier, per-model trip scores from weighted signals (429 rate, p95 timeout rate, 5xx rate, token throughput drop) over sliding windows
Attribution: run probabilistic attribution to isolate highest-likelihood cause; fallback actions tied to attributed entity (eg. route to variant-b in same region or failover to region-secondary)
Action catalog: graded actions - soft degrade (lower-cost quantized model), regional reroute, rate-limit/queue, hard circuit open (deny new session creation)
Hysteresis and decay: dual-window approach (short aggressive detection window + longer decay window) to avoid flip-flop; decay uses exponential backoff per-class
Dark probes and canary reopen: after decay period, send low-percentage dark probes to candidate target(s); require N successful consecutive probes before full reopen
Safeguards: tenant-protective limits (min throughput preserved), SLA-aware overrides for enterprise customers, manual-override hooks in Console
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (staging): implement autosentinel as opt-in behind feature flag; test with synthetic traffic and perf replay (1 week)
Phase 1 (canary): enable for 5 low-risk tenants in us-west-2 for 2 weeks; monitor dashboards and error budgets
Phase 2 (ramped): increase to 25% of production tenants with automatic rollback on anomaly thresholds
Phase 3 (global): enable by default with emergency kill-switch; train SREs on playbook
Rollback criteria: repeatable oscillations >3 cycles/hr, increase in end-to-end 5xx >2.5% above baseline, or unexplained latency increases affecting P95
monitoring_and_alerting: New telemetry: trip_score per entity, action_event stream (action_id, timestamp, entity, reason), probe_success_rate
Dashboards: Autosentinel overview, per-region action heatmap, per-tenant impact panel
Alerts: high-frequency oscillation alert, unsuccessful-reopen alert, increase-in-5xx-following-action alert
Logging: link action_id to request traces in trace-log for fast RCA
testing_and_validation: Unit tests for trip score computation and attribution logic
Integration tests: simulate 429 cascade from model v1 and ensure reroute to model v2 within 300ms
Chaos tests: introduce intermittent region packet loss and validate dark-probe canary behavior
Load tests: verify that soft-degrade reduces per-token cost by expected amount without violating latency SLO
decisions: Use weighted-signal fusion (configurable weights) instead of single-metric thresholds to reduce noisy triggers
Implement soft-degrade to model variants before global regional failover to minimize data sovereignty concerns
Expose action overrides and manual reopen controls in Console for enterprise tenants
tradeoffs: Complexity vs stability: attribution + dark probes adds system complexity but reduces false positives compared to simple thresholds
Latency: additional attribution computation adds ~1-3ms per request path for real-time scoring; batch evaluation will be used for lower-latency-sensitive classes
Cost: dark-probes and extra telemetry increase NPU/TCO marginally; we accept this for improved availability and clearer RCA
